title: Ezekiel Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 39.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 39, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The command to prophesy against Gog is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who is the chief prince mentioned in Ezekiel 39?
questions.explanation: Gog is identified as the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal in the verse.

questions.question: What will happen to Gog according to Ezekiel 39?
questions.explanation: The Lord God declares that He is against Gog, indicating Gog's defeat.

questions.question: How much of Gog will be left according to Ezekiel 39?
questions.explanation: The verse states that only the sixth part of Gog will be left.

questions.question: From where will Gog come up according to Ezekiel 39?
questions.explanation: The Lord will cause Gog to come up from the north parts.

questions.question: What will happen to Gog's bow and arrows?
options: They will be given to Israel
questions.explanation: The Lord declares He will smite Gog's bow out of his left hand.

questions.question: What will Gog and his bands be given to, according to the Lord?
questions.explanation: The Lord says He will give Gog and his bands to the ravenous birds and beasts of the field.

questions.question: Where shall Gog fall according to Ezekiel 39?
questions.explanation: Gog shall fall upon the mountains of Israel as stated in the verse.

questions.question: What will the people of Israel do with the weapons?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they shall set on fire and burn the weapons.

questions.question: How long will the weapons be burned?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they shall burn the weapons with fire for seven years.

questions.question: What will the people of Israel take from the fields or forests?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that they shall take no wood out of the field nor cut down any out of the forests.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will send a fire on Magog.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the Lord will send a fire on Magog.

questions.question: True or False: Gog will be praised by the people of Israel.
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the heathen shall know that the Lord is the Holy One in Israel, not that Gog will be praised.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of Israel will be destroyed.
questions.explanation: The text does not say that the cities of Israel will be destroyed, but rather that the people will go forth from the cities.

questions.question: True or False: Gog will be victorious over Israel.
questions.explanation: The text indicates that Gog will fall and be defeated, not victorious.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will be called the valley where Gog will be buried?
questions.explanation: The valley where Gog will be buried is specifically named 'The valley of Hamongog' in Ezekiel 39:11.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 39:12 promise will happen if the house of Israel buries the dead?
options: They will be rewarded with land
They will be protected from enemies
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:12 states that the house of Israel shall be burying the dead to cleanse the land.

questions.question: Who will bury Gog and all his multitude?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:13 confirms that all the people of the land shall bury Gog and it will be a renown for them.

questions.question: What will happen after seven months according to Ezekiel 39:14?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:14 indicates that after seven months, men will search for those that remain to cleanse the land.

questions.question: What should passengers do when they see a man's bone according to Ezekiel 39:15?
options: Set up a sign by it
questions.correctAnswer: Set up a sign by it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:15 instructs that when a passenger sees a man's bone, he should set up a sign until the buriers can bury it.

questions.question: What is the name of the city mentioned in Ezekiel 39:16?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:16 states that the name of the city shall be Hamonah, which is connected to the burial practices described.

questions.question: What does God ask every feathered fowl and beast of the field to do in Ezekiel 39:17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:17 commands the fowl and beasts to gather for a great sacrifice that God will make.

questions.question: What will the fowl eat according to Ezekiel 39:18?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:18 specifies that the fowl will eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of princes.

questions.question: What will happen to the fowl and beasts at God's table according to Ezekiel 39:20?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:20 states that the fowl and beasts shall be filled at God's table with horses and chariots.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 39:5 say about Gog's fall?
options: He will fall in the mountains
He will fall in the open field
questions.correctAnswer: He will fall in the open field
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:5 states that Gog shall fall upon the open field as a proclamation from the Lord.

questions.question: What will happen to the weapons of Gog's armies according to Ezekiel 39:9?
options: They will be burned with fire
They will be given to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They will be burned with fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:9 tells that the cities of Israel will burn the weapons for seven years.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 39:8 say about the day that God has spoken of?
options: It is a day of judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:8 confirms that the day God has spoken of is indeed come and done.

questions.question: True or False: The valley of Hamongog is meant for the burial of Gog.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:11 clearly states that Gog will be buried in the valley of Hamongog.

questions.question: True or False: The house of Israel will only bury Gog for one month.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:12 states that the house of Israel will bury the dead for seven months.

questions.question: True or False: The fowl will eat bread and drink water at God's sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:18 specifies that the fowl will eat flesh and drink blood, not bread and water.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 39.

questions.question: What will the heathen see among them according to Ezekiel 39:21?
questions.explanation: The verse states that all the heathen shall see God's judgment that He has executed, indicating the display of divine justice. (Ezekiel 39:21)

questions.question: What will the house of Israel know from that day forward according to Ezekiel 39:22?
options: I am the LORD their God
questions.correctAnswer: I am the LORD their God
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the house of Israel shall know that the LORD is their God from that day onward. (Ezekiel 39:22)

questions.question: Why did the heathen know that the house of Israel went into captivity according to Ezekiel 39:23?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the heathen shall know the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, indicating the reason behind their punishment. (Ezekiel 39:23)

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do for Jacob in Ezekiel 39:25?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Lord will bring again the captivity of Jacob, showing His intention to restore His people. (Ezekiel 39:25)

questions.question: What will happen after the house of Israel has borne their shame according to Ezekiel 39:26?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that after bearing their shame, the house of Israel will dwell safely in their land, implying restoration. (Ezekiel 39:26)

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'glory' in Ezekiel 39:21 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Glory' in this context refers to God's honor and majesty that He displays among the nations, as indicated by the context of the verse. (Ezekiel 39:21)

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Ezekiel 39:21 when stating 'my judgment that I have executed'?
questions.explanation: The phrase demonstrates parallelism by contrasting God's glory with His judgment, emphasizing both aspects of His character. (Ezekiel 39:21)

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of captivity and restoration found in Ezekiel 39:25?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 30:3 speaks about the return of Israel from captivity, connecting to the promise of restoration in Ezekiel 39:25. (Ezekiel 39:25)

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of God's spirit being poured out as mentioned in Ezekiel 39:29?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:4 describes the fulfillment of the promise of the Holy Spirit being poured out, mirroring the promise in Ezekiel 39:29. (Ezekiel 39:29)

questions.question: What comes immediately before Ezekiel 39:24?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:24 follows directly after verse 23, which discusses the reason for Israel's captivity. (Ezekiel 39:24)

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 39:29, what will God not do anymore?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 39:29, God declares that He will not hide His face from Israel anymore, signifying His restored relationship with them. (Ezekiel 39:29)

questions.question: The word 'iniquity' in Ezekiel 39:23 conveys what concept?
questions.explanation: 'Iniquity' refers to sin or wrongdoing, which is the reason for the house of Israel's captivity as stated in the verse. (Ezekiel 39:23)

questions.question: Ezekiel 39:27 mentions that God will be sanctified in the sight of which groups?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that God will be sanctified in the sight of many nations, demonstrating His power and holiness. (Ezekiel 39:27)

questions.question: It is true that Ezekiel 39:28 states God caused Israel to be led into captivity?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:28 confirms that God caused Israel to be led into captivity among the heathen, acknowledging His sovereignty in their situation. (Ezekiel 39:28)

questions.question: Ezekiel 39:29 states that God has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel. Is this statement false?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:29 clearly states that God has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel, affirming His active presence with them. (Ezekiel 39:29)

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 39:7 teach about God's nature?
options: God's holiness and the vindication of His holy name
God's mercy in forgiving sin without justice
God's sovereignty limited to Israel only
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and the vindication of His holy name
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:7 states that God will make His holy name known and not allow it to be polluted, demonstrating His holiness and desire for His name to be vindicated among the nations.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 39:29 teach about salvation?
options: God pours out His Spirit to renew and restore His people
Salvation is based on human merit and works
The Spirit is withheld because of persistent sin
Salvation is only for Gentiles, not Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God pours out His Spirit to renew and restore His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:29 promises that God will no longer hide His face but will pour out His Spirit on Israel, indicating a doctrine of spiritual renewal and restoration as part of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 39:25 teach about God's covenant faithfulness?
options: God restores Israel despite their past unfaithfulness
God abandons His people permanently after judgment
God's covenant is conditional and can be nullified
God only preserves Israel for earthly prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God restores Israel despite their past unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:25 states God will bring back the captivity of Jacob and show mercy, reflecting His covenant faithfulness to restore Israel despite their sins.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 39:6 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's justice in punishing the careless
God's love for all nations equally
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in punishing the careless
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:6 describes God sending fire on Magog and those dwelling carelessly, demonstrating His justice in punishing wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 39:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:21 says God will set His glory among the heathen and show His judgment, highlighting the attribute of God's glory revealed in judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 39:8 connect to the broader biblical theme of eschatological fulfillment?
options: It declares the fulfillment of God's promised day of judgment
It anticipates a temporary exile with no final restoration
It denies any future hope beyond the present age
It focuses exclusively on historical events without eschatology
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the fulfillment of God's promised day of judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:8 confirms that the prophesied day of the Lord's judgment has come, connecting to the eschatological theme of final divine intervention.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 39:22 make regarding Israel's knowledge of God?
options: It anticipates the restored covenant knowledge after exile
It denies Israel will ever know God again
It predicts Israel's permanent rejection of God
It focuses on Gentile enlightenment only
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the restored covenant knowledge after exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:22 teaches that Israel will know the LORD their God from that day forward, reflecting the restoration of covenant knowledge after judgment and exile.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 39:12 and Ezekiel 39:14 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves purification of the land through removing impurity
Sanctification is only spiritual with no physical implications
Sanctification occurs instantly without ongoing effort
Sanctification means separation from community involvement
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves purification of the land through removing impurity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:12 and 39:14 describe the burial and cleansing of the land from dead bodies, showing sanctification includes physical purification of the land.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 39:23 and Ezekiel 39:24 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Divine judgment is a direct response to Israel's iniquity and transgressions
Human sin is irrelevant to God's actions
God hides His face only for innocent people
Judgment comes randomly without moral cause
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment is a direct response to Israel's iniquity and transgressions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:23–24 explain that Israel's captivity and judgment were due to their sin and uncleanness, showing a doctrinal link between sin and divine judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 39:17 and Ezekiel 39:20 teach about God's victory over evil?
options: God's victory results in a feast for creatures symbolizing total defeat of enemies
God's victory is limited to spiritual realms only
God ignores the defeat of evil forces
God's victory causes destruction without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God's victory results in a feast for creatures symbolizing total defeat of enemies
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:17 and 39:20 depict birds and beasts eating the flesh and blood of defeated warriors, symbolizing God's comprehensive victory over evil.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 39:9–10 teaches that the weapons burning for seven years is a literal waste of resources. What does Ezekiel 39:9–10 actually teach?
options: The burning symbolizes complete and long-lasting peace eliminating war
The burning means God endorses wastefulness and destruction
The burning is a myth with no theological significance
The burning shows Israel's inability to manage resources
questions.correctAnswer: The burning symbolizes complete and long-lasting peace eliminating war
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:9–10 describes burning weapons for seven years so no wood is taken from fields, symbolizing the permanent end of war and a time of peace.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 39:11 teach about the reality of judgment and its consequences?
options: God provides a specific burial place for the multitude defeated in judgment
Judgment has no physical or historical consequences
God ignores the fate of the wicked after judgment
Judgment results only in spiritual correction without death
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a specific burial place for the multitude defeated in judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:11 states God will give Gog a burial place in Israel, showing the tangible and solemn consequences of divine judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 39:28 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's faithfulness in restoring His people to their land
God's selective salvation for Gentiles only
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness in restoring His people to their land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:28 declares God will gather Israel back to their land and leave none behind, showing His faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 39:27 make regarding God's sanctification and witness to other nations?
options: God is sanctified in Israel visibly before many nations, affirming His universal sovereignty
God acts only in secret with no witness to nations
God's sanctification is limited to Israel alone without broader significance
God's actions lack any redemptive-historical meaning
questions.correctAnswer: God is sanctified in Israel visibly before many nations, affirming His universal sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:27 shows God becomes sanctified in Israel before many nations, linking His sanctification to a broader redemptive-historical witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 39:2 and Ezekiel 39:3 teach about divine sovereignty over human rebellion?
options: God controls even the power and weapons of rebellious leaders
Human rebellion is beyond God's control
God supports the rebellious leaders in their plans
Divine sovereignty is limited and ineffective
questions.correctAnswer: God controls even the power and weapons of rebellious leaders
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 39:2 speaks of God turning Gog back, and 39:3 describes God smiting his bow and arrows, showing God's sovereignty over rebellion and military power.
